A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A-VARC research. Their main text and appendices are readable, and retained methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and distribution-shift results, component ablations, class-incremental learning experiments, and model-size analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative attribution evaluation, comparator results, and smoothing/pruning sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed classifier retains likelihood smoothing, partial-scale candidate pruning, CCA finetuning, and the same three-stage inference configuration. Token-wise mutual information is renamed TMI without changing its definition. The added attribution-evaluation machinery and comparator implementations do not revise A-VARC itself.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-100, the same five distribution-shift datasets, and the first ten ImageNet classes for incremental learning. The appendix class lists are identical. New attribution tests and sensitivity studies extend analysis of existing coverage rather than introduce a new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds MeanFlow-based DC-MF(25) to Table 1, LIME and SHAP to the new quantitative explanation comparison in Table 3, and a DiT diffusion classifier to the incremental-learning comparison in Table 4. These substantially broaden comparator coverage; the earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: Efficiency evaluation changes from runtime, including diffusion times estimated for an A6000, to per-image GFLOPs. New attribution evaluation uses insertion/deletion AUC, masked token likelihoods, and 5,000 perturbations for LIME and SHAP. The added incremental-learning diffusion baseline uses DiT-S/2 trained for 2,000 epochs; existing ResNet and VAR training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B tests smoothing sample counts, noise magnitude, and smoothing during partial-scale pruning. Section 6.1 and Appendix C add quantitative attribution comparisons and insertion/deletion curves, while Figure 8 adds visual cases. The earlier component ablation, model-size analysis, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added smoothing sample counts and attribution perturbation budgets concern computation and evaluation design, rather than uncertainty estimation across repeated experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds DC-MF's 50.30% ImageNet accuracy, attribution AUCs, a 76.0% incremental-learning average for DC, and smoothing sensitivity results. TMI achieves insertion/deletion AUCs of 0.944/0.605 for A-VARC+. Runtime entries are replaced by GFLOPs. Existing classification accuracies remain unchanged, including A-VARC+'s 89.32% versus DC's 90.30%; the revised efficiency ratio is not a same-metric performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Equations 13–14 defining the mask-weighted token log-likelihood and associated normalized class posterior used for attribution evaluation. The original classifier equations and token-wise mutual-information definition remain substantively unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The headline claim changes from a 160-fold inference speedup to approximately 89-fold lower computational cost relative specifically to the DiT classifier. The abstract replaces its broad contrast with diffusion models with a contrast against discriminative classifiers and emphasizes replay-free incremental adaptation. The central efficient, explainable VAR-classifier contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 proposes a velocity-training mismatch as a possible explanation for MeanFlow's poor classification results. It also interprets reduced smoothing gains after CCA and explains how excessive noise can average semantically dissimilar samples. Existing interpretations of distribution-shift weaknesses, model-size tradeoffs, and failure cases are retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies an author-implementation repository link and documents Kernel SHAP, 5,000 attribution perturbations, and masking of precomputed token likelihoods. The earlier A6000 runtime-estimation disclosure disappears with runtime reporting. Existing subset-selection recipes, class lists, and classifier pseudocode remain unchanged. Repository availability is stated in the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to MeanFlow, LIME, SHAP, and RISE to position the new comparisons and attribution metrics. These are focused extensions; the dedicated related-work discussion and its account of earlier generative classifiers remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraphs, conclusion, and incremental-learning discussion receive targeted rewrites. V2 standardizes TMI terminology, renames Section 6.2, reorganizes the appendices, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most methodological and related-work prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds attribution and sensitivity tables, pruning and insertion/deletion plots, and another visual-explanation panel. Figure 2 replaces its runtime axis with GFLOPs; Tables 1–2 replace time columns, and the incremental-learning table gains a DC comparison. Earlier heatmaps and confusion matrices are retained and relocated, while appendix tables and surrounding text are substantially rearranged.

improvement.justification: V1 supports its central explainability claim primarily through visual examples; v2 adds a documented quantitative evaluation against LIME and SHAP. New sensitivity studies strengthen support for the inference choices, and added generative comparators better establish the scope of the findings. Implementation access information also improves reproducibility. Attribution evaluation remains a masked-likelihood approximation, and removing runtimes sacrifices direct latency evidence, but the added validation substantially strengthens the paper overall.
